caption: why does the bell ring when I open my window 🔔
logline: Every time a Saltmouth kid opens his bedroom window, the village bell outside rings and the whole village runs indoors; tonight he leans out past the bell to see who rings it.
question: why does the bell ring every time he opens his window?
premise: For three hundred nights, every time the kid opens his upstairs window, the village bell right outside it rings and every villager runs inside. Nobody's ever there. Mom: 'Shutters SHUT, honey.' Every morning there's an arrow in the bell post, which Mom pulls out. By day every window in the village is open except his. Up on the cliff, under an old oak, something white stands all day. Tonight the bell rings again and he leans out past it to see who rings it.
twist: Nobody rings the bell. A skeleton lives in the shade of the oak on the cliff (skeletons shelter from the sun) and shoots at the only player in the village whenever he shows himself: the kid at his open window. The bell hangs on the arrow's line between the oak and his window, so every arrow hits the bell (vanilla: a projectile rings a bell; a rung bell sends villagers indoors). The bell was a shield. Tonight he leans out past it, and the skeleton draws on him with nothing in between. Cut on the draw.
